subject: Renewal negotiation — capacity conversion & credit swap
messages:

Cc: Sasha Romero <sasha.romero@emeraldtech.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal discussion: 2027-2028 contract & capacity plan

Hi Chloe,

We're kicking off our renewal planning for the July 1 renewal window and wanted to surface a couple of items before the formal renewal conversation. Current commit: 4 dedicated GPU nodes (p3-equivalent) with a 12-month term. Usage in Q1/Q2 has been uneven — we have predictable spikes and a moderate baseline.

Two asks on our side:
- Can we convert any unused committed capacity from the current contract into a one-time credit we can apply against Q3-Q4 consumption?
- Would Redwood consider a temporary price hold (6-9 months) for the renewed term while we finalize product integrations? A predictable unit price for that window would help our finance team.

We ran a quick usage export and attached our Q2 report for context. Ideally we'd like a preliminary commercial outline by next Wednesday so procurement and engineering can align.

Attachments: [attachment: Emerald_Q2_usage_report.xlsx (xlsx, 45KB)]

Thanks —
Phil Barnes

Date: 2027-04-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: 2027-2028 contract & capacity plan

Hi Phil — thanks for the heads up and the Q2 file, that helps a lot. We're happy to explore options that get EmeraldTech predictable economics while keeping performance solid.

Broadly, two commercial approaches look feasible from our side:
1) Credit conversion: convert a portion of unused committed spend into a one-time credit applied against usage over the next two quarters. Typical conversion rates range 8–15% depending on term and volume.
2) Short-term price hold: lock current unit rates for a 6-month window post-renewal, with a defined uplift thereafter tied to usage growth.

I've attached a draft proposal with numbers (redwood-proposal-v3.xlsx). Can we set a 30–45 minute call early next week (I’m available Tue/Wed morning PT) so we can agree on ranges and I can loop in renewals for final terms? If you have a target conversion % in mind, send that along and I’ll model it.

Attachments: [attachment: redwood-proposal-v3.xlsx (xlsx, 38KB)]

Best,

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-13T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: EmeraldTech renewal pricing options

Chloe / Ben / Lauren —

Quick modelling after Chloe’s note and the Emerald usage file. Key assumptions: current committed spend equivalent to $360k/yr; Q2 shows ~22% unused capacity on a run-rate basis.

Options we can propose (high-level):
- Option A (conservative): 10% conversion credit on unused committed spend + 6-month price hold at current unit rate. Estimated revenue impact: ~-2.4% over 12 months.
- Option B (commercial sweet spot): 12% conversion credit + 6-month hold + 3% uplift after hold. Impact: ~-3.1% but reduces churn risk and preserves committed floor.
- Option C (aggressive): 15% credit + 9-month hold — requires SDR/VP approval for >12% credit. Impact: -4.6%.

Recommend we present Option B as the default, call out Option A as fallback, and reserve Option C for exec escalation if procurement pushes. Ben — confirm technical compatibility for temporary capacity redistribution (burst policy) so we can propose a smooth conversion path. Lauren — if we present Option B, can renewals sign off on a 12% credit threshold or do we need explicit VP approval?

Attaching a quick impact model.

Attachments: [attachment: renewal-impact-model.csv (csv, 12KB)]

Thanks,
Vivek
Head of Sales Strategy
Redwood Inference
From: Phil Barnes <phil.barnes@emeraldtech.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Sasha Romero <sasha.romero@emeraldtech.com>, procurement@emeraldtech.com
Date: 2027-04-15T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: 2027-2028 contract & capacity plan

Chloe — appreciate the fast turnaround and the model. After an internal review, Emerald's ask is slightly different:

- We're targeting a 15% conversion credit on unused committed capacity (we believe this is reasonable given the uneven utilization last year).
- We'd like a 9-month price hold after renewal (to cover our integration and forecasting window).
- One-time onboarding credit of $25k to help offset migration costs for a planned integration in Q3.

If Redwood can meet those three items, procurement can sign a rolling 12-month renewal with the revised commit schedule. Otherwise procurement is pushing for a deeper overall discount.

We'd prefer to get a DocuSign link and a final commercial term sheet by Monday (2027-04-19) to stay on our internal timeline.

Thanks —
Phil
Dir of ML Platforms
EmeraldTech

Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: 2027-2028 contract & capacity plan

Phil — thanks — and thanks for laying out a clear path. Quick summary of what we can commit to and next steps: 

- Approved commercial: 12% one-time conversion credit on unused committed spend (applied as a credit across Q3-Q4 consumption).
- Price hold: 6 months at current unit rates.
- One-time onboarding credit: we can offer $15k. For the incremental ask (15% credit, 9-month hold, $25k onboarding), I can escalate to my VP for consideration — we want to be constructive but also need to preserve a minimum committed floor.

If that sounds OK, I'll have Renewals prepare a term sheet and DocuSign packet today. If procurement requires escalation, please confirm which line item (credit % or hold length or onboarding amount) is the priority so I can take a clear ask to my VP.
